RETRY TELEMETRY: atomic_io.replace_atomic emits one structured jsonl line per try (op/target/attempt/outcome/error/elapsed_ms/ts) to artifacts/io_events.jsonl — clean first-try successes stay silent, every retry/exhaustion/non-contention raises a line; the sink never breaks a state save. EMERGENCY RESTORE: restore_state.py replays applied auto_adjust telemetry events into the guard state — factor anchored at the newest before_gf (the ledger's own restore-target convention), ledger rows land as DATA through profit_guard._save (no apply_adjustment call, no multiplication), idempotent under replay; the drive's MUTATION pin proves the double-apply shape (anchor after_gf) reads 0.8336 and fails. LINTER IN THE GATE: diag_statewriters (R1 unregistered / R2 non-atomic / R3 resurrection) runs as test_statewriters.py on every commit touching the writer surface; the diag now recognizes atomic_io.replace_atomic as the rename, documents delegation (the op one-shots delegate to _save_contest_watch), and environment-skips bot writers when the sibling repo is absent (sandboxes). test_commitgate's expected-drive census now DERIVES from the hook's trigger matrix for the staged set instead of a frozen count. RUNBOOK: playbooks/state_file_recovery.md — named-contention and torn-JSON procedures with exact commands, the cross-platform rename-semantics matrix (NFS/SBM verdict: never host the tree on a network mount), the advisory-lock DECISION (rejected, with the revisit trigger), chaos cadence (every commit + Tuesdays + after environment drift), gate budget rules (split, never widen), and secrets handling. Explicitly NOT done: LockFileEx/fcntl (decision in the runbook) and NFS support (out of contract). Drives: statewriters 9/0, resilience 15/0, atomicio 8/0, profitguard 77/0, tidelearn 11/0, stateclobber 21/0, commitgate 70/0 x7.

28-round4-triage.title: ROUND 4 TRIAGED: THE WIPE TOMBSTONES, THE WRAP IS DEAD, THE RESTORE LEDGER IS COMPLETE, AND THE CLOCK IS SELF-RELIANT (Sep 29, round4-triage)
28-round4-triage.detail: The 004e2cc post-commit review's 12 findings, triaged. FIXED: (1) contest_account.new_contest's wipe lands TOMBSTONES read from the SAME file it writes (beside STATE_FILE — the round-3-style scanner-loader shortcut would leak foreign rows into a sandbox's wipe; my own first fix had this bug and the probe caught it), so a writer mid-RMW can no longer overlay stale rows back over the wipe (contest_window 38/1 -> 39/0). (2) per_gate_export's rotation ids WRAP, NEVER MODULO-24: the scanner stamps '20-24', a '%24' renders '20-00' which matches zero journal rows — default_rotation_id and full_rotation_id both corrected, pins updated (the review's major). (3) restore_state's replayed ledger rows carry rotation_id/status/day (the round-3 finding's field set) so the daily cap and the zone-4 wire read them. (4) atomic_io.TELEMETRY_PATH resolves from the module's directory, not the process cwd (a headless job started elsewhere would silently split the telemetry). (5) per_gate_export's clock is ZONEINFO-FIRST — reaching into app._now_mst pulled Streamlit into headless jobs and circular-imports. (6) the runbook's chaos-cadence section now matches the hook's real trigger mapping (no phantom Tuesday scheduler). TRIAGED, NOT FIXED: exit_extension:339 'active window suppresses the trail' is STALE — the seam suppresses the exit ACTION while the incumbent trail keeps re-firing each tick and remains the enforced stop (the docstring's contract, exit_extension 58/0 pins it); the launch_stack hindsight-failure semantics and app.py's capture median need operator decisions, recorded here as open. Drives: pergate 17/0, contest_window 39/0, resilience 15/0, tidelearn 11/0, topfill 13/0, statewriters 9/0.

29-giveback-ledger.title: THE GIVE-BACK LEDGER: THE DAY'S PEAK IS WATERMARKED, THE EROSION LEADS THE VOICE, AND A REALIZED SWING TIGHTENS THE GUARD ONCE (Sep 29, giveback-ledger)
29-giveback-ledger.detail: The user report: "Gave back $100 but doesn't count it? We were up $100 today, now we are back to +$2 — nothing adjusted. Says 'All Good' without checking what we gave back first." TRIAGE: the swing was REALIZED (the account went negative intraday and recovered); the ground truth showed +$39.44 banked total with only +$4.62 in applied journal rows — the gap is the open book's swing plus the window's prior carries — and NOTHING in the stack measured a day's peak-to-trough: the gauges sum realized rows, the danger machinery only reacts to losses vs the START balance, and the per-pair give-back warning (GIVEBACK_WARN_PCT_OF_SIZE, Sep 1) dies with each row's close. THE FIX, four layers: (1) _today_realized_pnl — the shared realized sum. (2) _track_day_giveback — a day-peak watermark (realized + unrealized, fed the exit cycle's per-row usd sum every tick, BEFORE the exit early-return so a full-exit tick updates the give-back) persisted in profit_guard_state under 'giveback'; past the $50 trigger it tightens the guard ONCE through auto_adjust.apply_adjustment — the PROTECTIVE direction (negative delta = factor down = tighter trail; the only direction the machine admits, verified against its non_negative_delta_is_not_self_adjust rail) — one attempt per day whatever the outcome (applied/queued/refused all land a ledger row; refusals never re-fire), telemetry emitted, rotation_id giveback-<day>. (3) _all_good_lead rewritten: the erosion LEADS ("Gave back 95 dollars from the day's peak — we were up 100, now plus 5") and 'All good' never prefixes it; the realized pace clause rides after; under the $25 speak floor the line stays All good. (4) PINS in test_allgoodlead (now 26 checks): the lead shape, the never-lie rule, the small-erosion silence, the tracker's protective direction, and the no-refire — with the guard state SANDBOXED via STATE_FILE and apply_adjustment mocked (the live scanner's state was never touched). Drives: allgoodlead 26/0, persistexit DONE, autotrack 43/43, trailstop 27/0, rebootsurv 25/0, profitguard 77/0, boundaryexam 35/0. PENDING: the running scanner (pid from scanner_pulse.json) picks the ledger up on its next restart.

32-panel-escaping.title: THE HINDSIGHT PANEL ESCAPES ITS PAYLOADS: A HOSTILE LEDGER ROW RENDERS AS INERT TEXT, PROVEN RED-FIRST (Sep 29, panel-escaping)
32-panel-escaping.detail: The round-5 review's XSS-class finding on the zones-4/5 wire slice, fixed and pinned. app.py grows _esc (html.escape with quote=True, None-safe) and EVERY payload-derived value in the API panel now passes through it: the rotation summary's proposed_reason, the gates' gate names and top-candidate pairs, the ledger's day/rotation_id/status/reason, the telemetry's rotation_id/status/applied_by/commit_sha/evidence_checksum/reason. The panel's own chrome (layout divs) stays raw — escaping is scoped to values. PINS (apptest 306/0): a hostile-payload matrix (script/img/svg/u/b/i tags across rotation_id, status, reason, applied_by, commit_sha, candidate pair) rides the existing stub-API harness and proves (a) no raw payload tag appears in any rendered markdown or expander label, (b) the values still render ESCAPED and readable (<script> visible — the operator sees the hostile row without it executing), (c) the panel chrome still renders raw. Red-first: the raw f-string interpolation failed the inert-text pin with verbatim . BONUS: the exception-handler census caught two bare except:pass left by the giveback edit — now named debug logs (scanner-state merge read, giveback telemetry skip). Also caught and fixed during this change: the _esc insertion had stolen _cached_api_path's @st.cache_data decorator (the pins' cache.clear() blew up — the census of my own harness worked). Drives: apptest 306/0, allgoodlead 26/0, stateclobber 21/0, statewriters 9/0.

33-round5-triage.title: ROUND 5 TRIAGED: THE RE-ADD HOLE, THE TELEMETRY TIMESTAMP, THE ZERO-PEAK EDGE, AND THE DRIVE'S OWN SINK SEAM (Sep 29, round5-triage)
33-round5-triage.detail: The 87565a7 post-commit review's 11 findings, triaged. FIXED: (1) MAJOR background_scanner._save_contest_watch — the raw tombstone rule silently dropped the FIRST deliberate re-add of a wiped pair (the exact SOLD-then-never-re-entered INJ scenario): _save_contest_watch grows fresh_keys, and the auto-track names the pair it is deliberately adding, so a popup-promised re-add lands on the first attempt while stale carriers stay suppressed — intent comes from the caller, the file cannot infer it. (2) MAJOR test_allgoodlead — the tracker legs wrote a fake applied giveback event into the LIVE telemetry journal (3 polluted rows found and purged); the drive now redirects telemetry_adjust.TELEMETRY_PATH into its tempdir and restores it in finally. (3) app.py — the telemetry TIMESTAMP (the one field missed by 32-panel-escaping) is escaped too. (4) MINOR background_scanner — a day opening AT peak 0.0 no longer freezes the give-back watermark (only an ABSENT peak counts as 'no peak yet'). SKIPPED, already-closed or by-design: the older ledger-fed panel's fields come from the machine's own journal (not the API wire; the API panel is the hostile-data surface); _flipgrade is the Sep-27-stale ledger line; the remaining drive-hygiene minors (simsweep grouping copy, commitgate no-leak scope, protected-extension exit-code, spec contradictions) are real but cosmetic and queue behind the majors. 36-fleet-sweep-tool.title: THE FLEET SWEEP IS A TOOL: ops/fleet_sweep.py RUNS EVERY DRIVE AND WRITES THE HTML HEALTH REPORT (Sep 29, fleet-sweep-tool)
36-fleet-sweep-tool.detail: The Sep-29 manual sweep (157 drives, the first 157->153+4 read) is now a repeatable operator tool. ops/fleet_sweep.py: discovers test_*.py in the root, runs sequentially (-X utf8, per-drive --timeout, default 240s), parses the house verdict conventions (RESULT N/M, x/y passed, ALL PASS, DONE), classifies failures against ops/fleet_sweep_classes.json (a reviewed file: status FLAKY|STALE_PIN + note + verified date; a failing drive WITHOUT an entry is RED — the tool never masks new failures), and writes artifacts/fleet_sweep/fleet_sweep_<stamp>.html + fleet_sweep_latest.html (self-contained dark report: GREEN/CLASSIFIED/RED cards, checks-passed count, per-drive table with failing-check excerpts) + fleet_sweep_last.json (machine-readable for trend diffs). Subset mode: ops/fleet_sweep.py test_tide canary. Exit 0 unless an UNCLASSIFIED failure exists — the commit gate stays the enforcement layer, this is the operators eyes. Classification debt renders AMBER with its verified date so stale classifications are visible as stale.

37-canary-simdefault.title: THE CANARY WHAT-IF STOPS TOUCHING PRODUCTION: RUN_CANARY DEFAULTS TO A PURE SIMULATION, ARM=TRUE IS THE STAGING EXERCISE (Sep 29, canary-simdefault)
37-canary-simdefault.detail: The four-review CodeRabbit major verified REAL from the code: run_canary unconditionally flip_canaryed, so any what-if run RE-ARMED the live cohort, STRIPPED the params cell the gate selected (flip writes a fresh doc), and a simulated breach would have rolled the LIVE cohort off. Default arm=False is now a pure simulation: no flip (record dial None), a breach REPORTS rollback_required=True without executing it, a pass reads pass_simulated — the live-style cohort doc (id, armed_at, AND the params cell alpha/delta_max/daily_cap) and the operators dial survive a simulated run BYTE-EXACT (pinned). arm=True keeps the real flip + real rollback, proven by a new sandboxed staging leg. The production arming path (ops/canary_enable -> flip_canary(params=...)) is untouched. test_canary 13 -> 15 checks; hindsightapi 41/0 and autoadjust 30/0 unaffected.
